config.title: Undo/Redo

intro.title: Undo/Redo
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple text editor that allows users to undo and redo their changes. You will learn how to implement this feature using a stack-based approach to track the history of user actions. The main technologies involved are Vue's reactive state management and JavaScript arrays to store the history. By the end, you'll understand how to manage state changes and provide a seamless user experience with undo/redo functionality.
intro.usecase: The undo/redo pattern is essential in any application where users make sequential changes they might want to reverse or reapply. You'll see this implemented in text editors like Google Docs for editing text, in design tools like Figma for adjusting visual elements, and in form-based applications where users might accidentally delete or modify important data. As a developer, you'll implement this pattern whenever you need to give users confidence to explore and modify content without fear of making permanent mistakes.

objectives: Implement a reactive history stack to track state changes
Construct undo and redo functions that manipulate the history stack
Initialize Vue component state with current position and history data
Bind undo/redo actions to UI buttons with appropriate event handlers
Control button states (enabled/disabled) based on history position
Update the application interface to reflect the current state from history
Integrate keyboard shortcuts for undo (Ctrl+Z) and redo (Ctrl+Y)

steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are available for use in your component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported something, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports aren't quite right. You need to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named UndoRedoDemo that uses the Composition API with the setup function. The component should return an empty template for now.
steps.hint: Define a component that exports a default object with a setup function. The setup function should return an empty object.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a Vue component structure ready to build the undo/redo functionality.
successCriteria: A component named UndoRedoDemo is created with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named UndoRedoDemo with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a Vue component named UndoRedoDemo with a setup function that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize the current text state
steps.instruction: Inside your Vue component, use the imported `ref` function to create a reactive state variable named `currentText` and initialize it with an empty string.
steps.hint: Call `ref('')` and assign it to a `const` variable named `currentText`.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a reactive state variable
const message = ref('Hello');
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive state variable `currentText` is created and ready to store the user's text input.
successCriteria: The component contains a `currentText` variable declared with `ref('')`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using `ref('')` to initialize an empty string state.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to create a `currentText` variable using `ref('')` inside your component.

steps.title: Initialize the history array state
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a reactive history array using ref and initialize it with an empty string as its first element.
steps.hint: Use ref to create a reactive array. Pass [''] as the initial value to ref.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a reactive array for history
const history = ref(['']);
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive history array is created and initialized with one empty string element.
successCriteria: The component contains a history array created with ref, initialized with [''].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref to create a reactive array and initializing it with an empty string inside an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to create a reactive history array using ref and initialize it with [''].

steps.title: Initialize the current index state
steps.instruction: Inside your component, use ref to create a reactive state variable named currentIndex and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: This will track which position in the history array we're currently viewing. Use the same pattern as the previous state variables.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a reactive index state
const currentIndex = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a currentIndex reactive state variable that starts at 0, ready to track the current position in the undo/redo history.
successCriteria: A currentIndex variable is created using ref() and initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using ref() and initializing currentIndex to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a reactive currentIndex state variable initialized to 0 using ref().

steps.title: Define the handleInput handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleInput that takes an event parameter, updates currentText with the event's target value, and pushes the new value to the history array.
steps.hint: Create a function that updates the reactive state. Use event.target.value to get the input text.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleInput function that updates currentText and adds to history when called with an input event.
successCriteria: The handleInput function is defined, updates currentText.value with event.target.value, and pushes the new value to history.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it updates both currentText and history correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleInput function is missing or doesn't update the state properly. Check the function definition and state updates.

steps.title: Define the undo handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleUndo that moves backward through history when called.
steps.hint: Create a function that checks if you can undo (currentIndex > 0), decrements currentIndex, and updates currentText from the history array at the new index.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleUndo function will allow moving backward through the history array when triggered.
successCriteria: A function named handleUndo is defined that decrements currentIndex and updates currentText from history when currentIndex > 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly checks if undo is possible (currentIndex > 0) and updates both currentIndex and currentText from the history array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The undo handler isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleUndo that moves backward through the history when possible.

steps.title: Define the redo handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleRedo that increments currentIndex and updates currentText from the history array.
steps.hint: Check if there is a future state in history (currentIndex < history.value.length - 1). If so, increment currentIndex and set currentText to the corresponding history value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleRedo function will be defined and ready to be called when a redo action is triggered.
successCriteria: A function named handleRedo is defined that checks for a future state, increments currentIndex, and updates currentText from history.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleRedo function properly checks if there's a future state (currentIndex < history.value.length - 1) and updates both currentIndex and currentText.
steps.feedbackWrong: The redo handler isn't quite right. Remember to check if there's a future state available, then increment currentIndex and set currentText to the corresponding value from history.

steps.title: Create the main template structure
steps.instruction: Return a template from your Vue component with a container div and a heading that says 'Undo/Redo Text Editor'.
steps.hint: In Vue, the template is returned from the component's setup function. Use a div with a class and an h1 heading.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a template with a container div and a heading, establishing the basic UI structure.
successCriteria: The component returns a template containing a div with a class and an h1 with the text 'Undo/Redo Text Editor'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your template includes a div with a class and an h1 heading with the correct text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is missing or incorrect. Check that you're returning a template with a div and an h1.

steps.title: Add the text input and wire it to handleInput
steps.instruction: In the template, add a text input element. Bind its value to currentText and its input event to handleInput.
steps.hint: Use v-model for two-way binding or v-bind:value and @input to connect the input to your state and handler.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: text input with binding -->
<input type="text" v-model="message" @input="updateMessage" />
steps.expectedOutcome: A text input field appears in the template, connected to the currentText state and handleInput handler.
successCriteria: The template contains an input element with value bound to currentText and input event bound to handleInput.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input, but check the binding. Make sure value is currentText and input event calls handleInput.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input is missing or not properly connected. Review how to bind input values and events in Vue.

steps.title: Add the undo button and wire it to the undo handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Undo' inside your template, and bind its click event to the undo handler function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag with @click directive to call the undo handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="handleUndo">Undo</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Undo' appears in the UI, and clicking it will trigger the undo functionality.
successCriteria: A <button> element with 'Undo' text and @click binding to the undo handler is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text 'Undo' and the @click directive calls the undo handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Undo button is missing or incorrectly implemented. Add a <button> with text 'Undo' and @click binding to the undo handler.

steps.title: Add the redo button and wire it to the redo handler
steps.instruction: Add a 'Redo' button next to the undo button in your template and wire its click event to the handleRedo function.
steps.hint: Add a button element with text 'Redo' and use @click to call handleRedo.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="handleAction">Action</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Redo' button appears next to the 'Undo' button that triggers the redo functionality when clicked.
successCriteria: The template contains a button with text 'Redo' and its click event is bound to handleRedo.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the text 'Redo' and uses @click="handleRedo" to call the redo handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The redo button isn't properly implemented. Add a button element with 'Redo' text and bind its click event to handleRedo.
